Overall tone: slightly positive but cautious. The FOMC highlights a strong labor market and solid household spending, yet flags weak business investment and exports and inflation running below 2%. The rate cut to 1.5–1.75% and balance-sheet/overnight operations to maintain ample reserves are consistent with evidence that monetary policy affects real activity (Sims, 1992) and with an inflation-targeting approach that places weight on inflation expectations (Svensson). With market-based inflation compensation low and surveys little changed (Bullard), easing is aligned with the mandate to stabilize inflation around the symmetric 2% goal. At the same time, academic work cautions against over-interpreting low unemployment given challenges matching labor-market behavior with simple labor-supply elasticities (Christiano and Eichenbaum; Chari, Kehoe, and McGrattan) and the potential for hysteresis (Philippopoulos, Jonsson, Svensson), which, together with global uncertainties and FOMC dissents, tempers the positive tone.
